subject: Dedicated sizing: surge traffic workbook & prompt mix
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@orionai.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-team@orionai.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood sizing help — upcoming launch; sample telemetry attached

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking this — we have an initial product launch in Q1 and expect a big first-week surge. Quick context: OrionAI is moving a new assistant from a small pilot (approx 600 daily active users) to a public preview targeting 25k daily active users with a heavy daytime concentration in US Pacific hours.

Attached is a small telemetry extract (orion_telemetry_sample.csv) showing recent prompt/response profiles from the pilot. Top-line asks: can Redwood help us estimate dedicated fleet sizing (reserved GPUs) to meet p95 generation latency <= 700ms and sustain burst windows up to 10x baseline for 30–90 minute windows? We also need guidance on prompt vs response token mix and whether session affinity / KV cache will materially change sizing.

A couple quick clarifications we can provide now:
- Primary model: open-model-v2-70B (we're evaluating quantized variants)
- Typical prompt length: 30–120 tokens (median ~50)
- Typical response length: 60–400 tokens (median ~220)
- Expected concurrency at baseline: ~120 concurrent sessions, with peak bursts targeting ~1,500 concurrent sessions for short windows

Can you send a short worksheet/questionnaire for the pre-sales sizing? We'd like a ballpark before scheduling a sizing workshop.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Director of Platform Engineering
OrionAI

Attachments: orion_telemetry_sample.csv (CSV, 112 KB)
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena@orionai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood sizing help — upcoming launch; sample telemetry attached

Elena — thanks for the telemetry and the clear context. Appreciate the prompt/response stats; that'll help a lot. I'm attaching a concise pre-sales workbook below (inline questions) that our sizing team uses to produce a draft capacity plan. If you can fill the highlights we can run a first-pass projection and propose a short 60‑minute sizing workshop to align on assumptions.

Short worksheet (please reply inline or attach answers):
1) Workload shape
   - Baseline daily active users and expected DAU at launch: (you sent 25k; please confirm expected weekly distribution)
   - Peak burst multiplier: what's the multiplier and expected duration for the largest burst (you noted 10x for 30–90m; confirm start times/timezones)
2) Session details
   - Avg prompt tokens and 95th percentile prompt tokens (if available)
   - Avg response tokens and 95th percentile response tokens
   - Chat vs single-turn usage % (e.g., 70% chat, 30% single prompt)
3) Concurrency and sessions
   - Typical session concurrency baseline and expected peak concurrency during burst windows
   - Are sessions sticky to model instances (session affinity), or are requests stateless?
4) Latency SLOs
   - P50/P95 generation target (you said p95 <= 700ms; confirm p50 goal and whether end-to-end includes network)
5) Model/quantization
   - Exact model variant and quantization you plan to use (float16, int8, etc.)
   - Are you open to a smaller model variant for cost/latency tradeoffs?
6) Fallbacks and degrade modes
   - If capacity is constrained, are fallbacks to a smaller model acceptable? Any hard constraints on output fidelity?
7) Traffic patterns and geo
   - Daypart distribution (hours with high traffic), and whether traffic is concentrated in a single region (you mentioned US-PAC).
8) Telemetry artifacts
   - If possible, provide token-level histograms, sample traces showing request arrival timestamps (to simulate burst shape), and any KV cache hit-rate estimates.

What we'll deliver after your responses: a one-page dedicated sizing estimate (GPU SKUs, reserved capacity bands, estimated sustained & burst throughput, recommended batch sizing, and recommended KV cache settings), an estimated monthly cost band, and a short agenda for the workshop.

I'll loop in Marissa for the sizing math and Ben for cost assumptions. Can we lock a 60‑minute slot next week for the workshop? I'm free Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pre-sales-sizing-workbook.pdf (worksheet template)
From: Elena Torres <elena@orionai.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-team@orionai.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood sizing help — upcoming launch; sample telemetry attached

Vivek — thanks, filled quick answers inline below and attached a short prompt-mix summary (prompt-mix-summary.pdf). I've also included a small arrival-time sample to show burst shape.

Inline answers:
1) Workload shape
   - DAU expected at preview launch: 25,000 (week 1). We expect a strong M-F daytime concentration; weekends ~30% of weekdays.
   - Peak burst multiplier: 8–12x baseline; the largest observed burst during pilot was ~9x for 45 minutes starting around 10:30am PT.
2) Session details
   - Avg prompt tokens: 52; p95 prompt tokens: 118
   - Avg response tokens: 210; p95 response tokens: 380
   - Chat vs single-turn: ~85% multi-turn chat, 15% single-turn
3) Concurrency and sessions
   - Baseline concurrency: 120; expected peak concurrent sessions during large bursts: 1,050–1,800 (we plan conservative assumption of 1,500)
   - Sessions are moderately sticky; we maintain short-lived session affinity for context (KV cache hit-rate ~40% in pilot)
4) Latency SLOs
   - Targets: p50 ~220ms, p95 <=700ms (generation only); end-to-end includes network (we'll budget 100–150ms for edge latency)
5) Model/quantization
   - Model: open-model-v2-70B; prefer int8-quantized for cost but want analysis for float16 as baseline
   - We are open to evaluating a 30B variant if it meets fidelity thresholds
6) Fallbacks
   - Fallback to smaller model is acceptable for non-critical queries; some content (billing/account flows) must always use the primary model
7) Traffic patterns
   - Daypart: 9am–3pm PT heavy; secondary spike 6pm–8pm PT. Single-region (us-west) primary.
8) Telemetry
   - Attached token histograms and a 2-hour arrival sample (csv).

Let's lock Wed 11/25 1pm PT for the workshop (I'll book a 60‑minute slot). Can your sizing team run a draft by EOD Mon after the worksheet inputs?

Thanks,
Elena

Attachments: prompt-mix-summary.pdf (4 pages), burst-arrival-sample.csv (18 KB)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena@orionai.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood sizing help — upcoming launch; sample telemetry attached

Elena / team — thanks for the detailed answers and the artifacts; very helpful. We've started a quick first-pass projection and here's the short playbook we'll bring to the workshop:

- Draft capacity estimate (high-level): to meet p95 <=700ms for open-model-v2-70B (int8) with ~40% KV cache, estimate a reserved band of 12–18 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs for baseline + scheduled buffer, with burst elasticity up to ~28 GPUs via burst pool (this assumes aggressive batching during sustained periods and conservative batch sizes for sub-1s latency).
- If you opt for float16 the baseline moves toward 16–24 GPUs; if you choose a 30B model variant baseline is ~6–9 GPUs (with lower cost but lower fidelity).
- Recommendations we'll validate in the workshop: batch config (target token-batch 4–8k depending on response length), KV cache policy (pin recent sessions, TTL 30 minutes), and canary routing to test fallback model during spikes.

Deliverables before the workshop: 1-page slide with GPU bands & estimated monthly cost ranges, a short technical annex describing batching strategy and cache assumptions, and a proposed runbook for scaled bursts. We'll circulate EOD Mon PT as discussed.

See you 11/25 1pm PT — I'll share a calendar invite.

—Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: draft-capacity-notes.txt (attached to internal working doc)
